answer: Because the falcon audit recomputes usage from the vault history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a trivial one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 406 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A farm running 37 keys thus forfeits for 37 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the karst declaration. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
